l4_steps.name: Detect Warranty-Eligible Maintenance Event
l4_steps.input: Unscheduled removal, component failure report, or shop finding in AMOS
l4_steps.output: Potential warranty event flag on work order
l4_steps.kpi: Warranty event capture rate ≥95% of eligible removals
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS warranty flag relies on manual technician input; missed flags cause unrecoverable cost leakage when discovery exceeds OEM claim window (typically 90 days)

l4_steps.name: Validate Warranty Coverage Against OEM Contract
l4_steps.input: Component part number, serial number, date of manufacture, hours/cycles on wing
l4_steps.output: Coverage determination: in-scope / out-of-scope with contract reference
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage determination completed within 2 business days of event flag
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM warranty terms scattered across multiple Ariba contract line items; exclusions for airline-induced damage (e.g. FOD, corrosion) frequently disputed without clear documented threshold

l4_steps.name: Confirm Component Airworthiness History
l4_steps.input: Component serial number, operator-applied ADs, service bulletins, repair history
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness history extract confirming no owner-induced damage voiding coverage
l4_steps.kpi: History pull completed within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP component records can have gaps when aircraft are acquired from lessors or third-party MROs; incomplete records lead to OEM claim rejection citing unverifiable maintenance history

l4_steps.name: Gather Supporting Work Orders and Borescope Evidence
l4_steps.input: AMOS work order, shop finding report, borescope images, QA sign-off records
l4_steps.output: Documentation package: work orders, photographs, tear-down report
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation pack assembled within 5 business days of removal
l4_steps.pain_point: Borescope images stored outside AMOS in file shares; retrieval is manual and inconsistent — OEMs (CFM, Pratt & Whitney) require image sets in specific DPI/format standards or reject claims on technical grounds

l4_steps.name: Assess Documentation Completeness Against OEM Checklist
l4_steps.input: OEM warranty submission checklist, assembled documentation package
l4_steps.output: Gap list or complete sign-off for claim package
l4_steps.pain_point: Each OEM (Airbus, CFM, Honeywell, Collins Aerospace) has different checklist formats and portal requirements; maintaining current versions of each OEM's checklist is a manual process with no automated update feed

l4_steps.name: Build Formal Warranty Claim Package
l4_steps.input: Complete documentation set, contract reference, estimated recovery value
l4_steps.output: Formal warranty claim dossier with cover letter and cost quantification
l4_steps.kpi: Claim value accuracy within ±5% of final settlement
l4_steps.pain_point: Labour rate and material cost calculations reference SAP actuals — discrepancies between AMOS work order cost codes and SAP cost centres cause reconciliation errors that delay settlement

l4_steps.name: Submit Claim via OEM Vendor Portal
l4_steps.input: Completed claim dossier, OEM-specific portal credentials, part return authorisation (if required)
l4_steps.output: Claim reference number and submission confirmation from OEM portal
l4_steps.kpi: Claim submitted within 30 days of component removal (OEM SLA compliance)
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM portals (Airbus WSC, CFM TEAM, Honeywell MyAerospace) each have unique interfaces; no API integration with AMOS/Ramco means double-entry and high rework rate (~25%) for portal validation errors

l4_steps.name: Register Claim in Warranty Tracking Register
l4_steps.input: OEM claim reference, submission date, recovery value estimate, OEM SLA deadline
l4_steps.output: Warranty claim record with status, owner, and SLA timer in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of submitted claims logged within same business day
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS warranty module not universally adopted — some analysts maintain parallel spreadsheet trackers creating version drift and missed follow-up triggers

l4_steps.name: Monitor Claim Status and Escalate on SLA Breach
l4_steps.input: AMOS SLA timer alerts, OEM portal status updates
l4_steps.output: Escalation email or updated status flag if OEM response overdue
l4_steps.kpi: OEM response within 30-day SLA for standard claims; escalation triggered within 5 days of breach
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS SLA alerting requires manual daily review; no automated push notification to account managers — high-value claims (>$50K) routinely age past SLA without escalation

l4_steps.name: Review OEM Assessment and Determination
l4_steps.input: OEM written determination (accept / partial accept / reject), technical rationale
l4_steps.output: Internal review memo: accepted amount vs. claimed amount, variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Claim acceptance rate ≥70% of submitted value
l4_steps.pain_point: OEMs commonly invoke exclusion clauses (FAR Part 43 compliance gaps, improper storage, FOD) with limited technical substantiation — airline burden of proof is high and legal recourse under IATA ATA Spec 200 is slow

l4_steps.name: Escalate Disputed Claims to Commercial Team
l4_steps.input: Rejected or partially accepted claim, OEM determination letter, original contract terms
l4_steps.output: Formal dispute letter or escalation to OEM account executive via Ariba correspondence log
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute initiated within 10 business days of unsatisfactory determination
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with smaller fleets or lower OEM spend have limited commercial leverage — Boeing and CFM prioritise high-volume operators; dispute resolution timelines can exceed 180 days for turbine-module claims

l4_steps.name: Prepare Technical Counter-Evidence Package
l4_steps.input: OEM rejection rationale, component maintenance records, AD compliance evidence
l4_steps.output: Counter-evidence dossier with supplementary airworthiness and compliance data
l4_steps.kpi: Counter-evidence submitted within 15 business days of dispute initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: AD compliance records in CAMP may not cross-reference superseded bulletins; if OEM cites a service bulletin the airline cannot prove was complied with, the claim is unrecoverable

l4_steps.name: Process Approved Warranty Credit or Replacement Part
l4_steps.input: OEM approval letter, credit note or replacement part despatch notice
l4_steps.output: SAP credit memo posted to vendor account; or goods receipt for replacement component
l4_steps.kpi: Credit posted within 5 business days of OEM approval; replacement part receipted against correct maintenance order
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM credit notes issued in vendor's currency (USD, EUR) — FX timing differences between AMOS claim valuation and SAP posting date create unexplained P&L variance in MRO cost accounts

l4_steps.name: Close Claim and Update Warranty Register
l4_steps.input: SAP credit memo number or replacement goods receipt, final settlement amount
l4_steps.output: AMOS warranty record closed with actual recovery value, settlement date, and variance note
l4_steps.kpi: Claim closure within 3 business days of financial settlement; register accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS closure step is often skipped when analysts are under workload pressure — open claim backlog inflates apparent recovery pipeline and distorts management reporting

l4_steps.name: Generate Warranty Recovery KPI Dashboard
l4_steps.input: AMOS warranty register export, SAP credit memo data, claim age data
l4_steps.output: Monthly warranty KPI report: recovery rate, claim cycle time, rejection rate by OEM
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by 5th business day of each month; warranty recovery rate ≥3.5% of total MRO spend
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-Tableau data pipeline is batch-refresh (T+1); real-time claim status not visible to Finance — monthly accruals for outstanding claims are estimated manually and frequently restated

l4_steps.name: Analyse Claim Patterns and Trigger Vendor Review
l4_steps.input: 12-month warranty claim dataset, component reliability data, OEM rejection rate trends
l4_steps.output: Vendor performance scorecard; recommendation for contract renegotiation or supplier change
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor review completed annually; rejection rate per OEM <15%; repeat claim rate on same part number <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Warranty rejection patterns (e.g. systemic CFM LEAP defect series) are not automatically correlated with fleet reliability data in Redshift — root cause identification requires manual cross-referencing across three systems
